title: RBAC v2 graceful switchover and audit preservation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Migration plan to move customers from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with minimal downtime and guaranteed preservation of audit trails. This ticket covers validation scripts, audit ETL, admin gating controls, SSO/SAML mapping checks, communications cadence, and rollback/runbook artifacts.
background: RBAC v2 introduces resource-scoped permissions and a normalized audit schema. v1 stores permission blobs and older audit records in a different shape. We must ensure that (1) existing admin workflows continue to work during the migration window, (2) audit fidelity is preserved and searchable post-migration, and (3) SSO role mappings continue to map to equivalent v2 roles. Several customer accounts have strict compliance requirements that prohibit any gap in audit logging.
goals: Enable a staged switch that allows v1 users to continue operating until v2 verification is complete
Preserve and surface historical audit events in the new schema without losing actor or context fields
Offer an automated verification report for each customer after migration completes
Provide a tested rollback path to v1 behavior within 30 minutes if critical issues arise
Communicate migration schedule and impact clearly to affected customers and account teams
tasks: Inventory v1 permission blobs and map to canonical v2 role definitions (mapping table + coverage gaps)
Implement a one-way audit ETL to normalize historical events into v2 audit schema and store with original raw payload as reference
Build and run reconciliation suite that compares effective permissions between v1 and v2 for sample sets and full-customer dry‑run
Ship dual-write mode for permission changes (v1 + v2) behind feature flag and test for eventual consistency
Add admin-console toggle to enable per-organization switchover (soft migration for pilots)
Validate SAML/SSO role assertion mappings against v2 role set and add translation layer for edge cases
Create migration smoke tests: auth flows, admin workflows, RBAC-enforced APIs, rate-limited routes
Create runbooks: pre-cutover checklist, post-cutover verification steps, rollback steps with health checks
Instrument dashboards: permission-drift metric, dual-write error rate, audit-ingest lag, search-hit retention
Draft and send customer communications and account playbook for enterprise customers (timeline, opt-out, support channels)
Coordinate cross-team review with Platform, Console, Support, and Legal for compliance sign-off
acceptance_criteria: Migration scripts produce deterministic v2 role assignments for >99.9% of users in pilot orgs
Historical audit events are queryable in Console and match v1 semantics for actor, resource, action, and timestamp (sampling verified)
Dual-write shows <0.01% write divergence at steady state across 48-hour staging test
Admin console per-org toggle works and can be reversed without requiring data reimport
SAML assertions for top 20 enterprise customers map to valid v2 roles or are flagged with clear remediation steps
Runbook rollback can be executed by on-call engineer and returns service to v1-equivalent authorization within 30 minutes in test drills
notes: Trade-off: full real-time migration of audit history increases migration time and I/O; we opt for batched ETL plus on-demand rehydration for very large accounts
Decision: store original v1 audit payloads as attachments to preserve raw provenance while surfacing normalized fields for search
Open question: whether to support legacy APIs indefinitely or deprecate after 6 months post-migration for simplicity
We will not attempt automatic 1:1 mapping for custom customer roles with free-form rules; these are surfaced in a remediation report and require manual review
